## Appendix A. Per-row catalogue disposition G-001..G-234

Source: framing candidate A, section 16 (unit run `unit-run-1792246479142-9f284c74/producer/1`). Every G-id appears exactly once. Unmodified rows carry the frozen obligation text of `plans/reports/research-261017-1032-git-lessons-catalogue.md` (Vietnamese, as frozen) as a requirement, not as proof of a passing test; legacy mechanisms in them remain subject to the precedence rule of §16. Rows in the 32 override groups of §16 have their Disposition and obligation cells replaced by the effective rule; RT2-F1 rows are marked “override per RT2-F1” and were confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-17.

| Lesson | Disposition / owning contract | Vector | Frozen obligation carried (legacy mechanism subject to disposition) |
|---|---|---|---|
| G-001 | Override per §16 G-001 / G-183; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Effective rule: Two named env contexts, one backend owner: scrubbed runner; validated hook-index context. |
| G-002 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Gitdir của worktree chỉ lấy từ con trỏ `worktrees/<name>/gitdir` của repo chính, khớp theo realpath với worktree; không bao giờ đọc từ `.git` của worktree. `repoRoot` phải là main checkout thật (cha của common-dir bằng chính nó); linked worktree, worktree không thuộc repo, hoặc thiếu `repoRoot` đều bị từ chối bằng `untrusted-worktree`. |
| G-003 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi git của runner mang `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. |
| G-004 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | `core.hooksPath` tương đối được resolve theo main checkout; đường dẫn tuyệt đối hoặc `~` giữ nguyên. Khi cài đặt, luôn ghi `core.hooksPath` tuyệt đối trỏ vào `.githooks` của main checkout. |
| G-005 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi merge của runner chạy với `rerere.enabled=false` và `merge.autoStash=false`. |
| G-006 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Dùng danh tính của chính repo; chỉ khi một trường chưa đặt mới dùng `fgOS runner <runner@fgos.local>`. |
| G-007 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Resolve base bằng `rev-parse -q --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`; kết quả null nghĩa là 'không trỏ tới commit nào' và bị từ chối trước khi có run. |
| G-008 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Lệnh con kết thúc theo sự kiện thoát của chính child trực tiếp, và timeout phải thực sự chặn được thao tác kể cả khi hậu duệ giữ descriptor. Rust cần quyết định có leo thang từ SIGTERM lên kill cả nhóm process hay không (code cũ không làm). |
| G-009 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lỗi git mang `stderr` và exit status qua mọi ranh giới trừu tượng (typed error/outcome); lỗi do tràn buffer thành lỗi nghiệp vụ có hướng dẫn ('sync/rebase it'); lỗi trong các hàm đọc ánh xạ về một mã validation thống nhất; probe cố ý fail-open thì nuốt stderr; nhánh fail-closed giữ nguyên nguyên nhân gốc. |
| G-010 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi nơi đọc danh sách path của git đều dùng `-z` và tách theo NUL: path đúng bằng byte git đặt tên, không trim; trong `status --porcelain=v1 -z` bản ghi có R hoặc C ở bất kỳ cột nào đọc thêm trường kế làm path thứ hai và trả cả hai nửa, khử trùng; `diff --name-status -z` đọc R/C thành hai path; bỏ dấu `/` cuối của thư mục untracked bị gộp; bỏ phần tử rỗng. |
| G-011 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Bộ đọc danh sách path có trần output 64 MiB; diff đầy đủ cho review có trần 50 MiB; hook đọc blob với buffer 200 MB; vượt trần phải báo thành lỗi chẩn đoán được, không phải ENOBUFS thô. Component Rust phải truyền dữ liệu theo luồng hoặc có ngưỡng tường minh tương đương. |
| G-012 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi `diff` trả danh sách path đều truyền `--no-relative`. |
| G-013 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi `status` đọc danh sách truyền tường minh `--untracked-files=all` (hoặc `normal` khi chỉ cần biết có bẩn hay không), bất kể config người dùng. |
| G-014 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Danh sách staged và changed-file dùng `--no-renames` để mỗi nửa được xét riêng; ngoại lệ duy nhất là `branchContentMismatch`, nơi chỉ cần tên mới nên bật detect rename. |
| G-015 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Pathspec luôn là literal: `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` cùng `--pathspec-from-file=-` phân tách NUL trên stdin (không giới hạn độ dài), hoặc `--literal-pathspecs`. |
| G-016 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | So sánh path checkout sau `realpath.native`, bỏ tiền tố mở rộng, chuẩn hóa dấu phân cách, không phân biệt hoa/thường trên win32; chạy executable theo ngữ nghĩa từng nền tảng (shell cho `.cmd`); kiểm tra liveness và định danh process đi qua một adapter nền tảng. |
| G-017 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Component mới dùng `-z` ở mọi nơi, kể cả `worktree list --porcelain -z`, để không có ngoại lệ nào phụ thuộc vào việc 'chỉ test rỗng'. |
| G-018 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Trunk là đích của `origin/HEAD`, nếu không có thì `main`/`master` cục bộ, cuối cùng mới là chữ `main`; tương tự bước workflow `integrate` phải nhận đích tường minh. Không nơi nào được viết cứng `main`; còn cần quyết định các nhãn `main` trong approve/catchup là chủ ý hay sót. |
| G-019 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Main checkout được nhận diện theo cấu trúc (git-dir bằng common-dir, toplevel), không theo registry. Đường dẫn không phải repo git coi là main (fail open, chưa có test). Root là tham số tường minh (`--dir`), cwd chỉ là ngữ cảnh. Verb ghi từ worktree không nối với store sống bị từ chối trừ khi có `--dir` trỏ main. |
| G-020 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Hàm ancestry ba giá trị: exit 1 nghĩa là không, mọi mã khác ném lỗi (`MergeError`). Cả sync, catchup, approve và cleanup dùng chung hàm này. |
| G-021 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | `isCheckoutDirty` fail-closed (lỗi nghĩa là bẩn) và loại `:!.fgos`; `checkoutDirtyPaths` (chỉ liệt kê) fail-open ra danh sách rỗng; độ bẩn khi resync được đánh giá so với commit đồng bộ gần nhất, không so với HEAD hiện tại. |
| G-022 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Parse stanza (`worktree `, `branch `, dòng trống) và trả realpath của checkout đang giữ branch, hoặc null. |
| G-023 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Tính `rev-parse --show-prefix` (chỉ cắt dấu xuống dòng vì tên có thể bắt đầu hay kết thúc bằng khoảng trắng) và so `.fgos` với tiền tố đó. |
| G-024 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Đọc tip của ref có tên bằng `rev-parse <ref>` từ repo root, không phải HEAD của worktree nào đó. |
| G-025 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Điểm đồng bộ của worktree là mục reflog mới nhất của chính HEAD (`reflog show HEAD -n 1`), không phải `rev-parse HEAD`; reflog hoặc tip không đọc được thì fail closed. |
| G-026 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Tìm MERGE_HEAD bằng `rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` (đúng cả trong linked worktree). Ba luật sở hữu (sync unit, approve/merge, hook) được giữ riêng ở các mục về sync và land. |
| G-027 | Override per §16 G-027; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Effective rule: Work owns claim reclaim **policy**. Git supplies facts (status, mtimes, branch tips) only. Do not claim reclaim in a Git facts row. |
| G-028 | Carry §3/6/11 worktree/custody/recovery | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Tái dùng branch `fgw/<id>` đã có (không bao giờ `-b` lại) và luôn cấp thư mục `mkdtemp` mới; nếu branch chưa tồn tại thì `-b <branch> <path> <baseRef>`; đường dẫn trả về là realpath. | G-029 | Partial retirement: event-file workaround gone; provisioning/non-event worktree rules retained §3/11 | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Sau mỗi checkout (và sau mọi `reset --hard`) xóa hẳn `.fgos/` khỏi worktree của worker. Nhánh worker không bao giờ tạo hay chở trạng thái control-plane. Đường workflow `createWorkflowWorktree` hiện không strip (xác minh `integrate.mjs:33-63`), component mới phải áp dụng cho mọi cửa tạo worktree. |
| G-030 | Override per §16 G-030 / G-031; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: **Execution**, after `worktree-create` returns, outside every Git lock. Git does not spawn `npm` or setup commands. |
| G-031 | Override per §16 G-030 / G-031; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: **Execution**, after `worktree-create` returns, outside every Git lock. Git does not spawn `npm` or setup commands. |
| G-032 | Override per §16 G-032; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: Git worktree-create ends at registration and the worker `.fgos` strip, then returns; it takes no `beforeProvision` callback. Execution provisions dependencies and runs setup after create returns, outside every Git lock (§1, G-030/G-031). Retained lesson: a lock is held only for the narrow Git metadata mutation, and nothing holds main while provisioning runs. (override per RT2-F1) |
| G-033 | Override per §16 G-033; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: Git rolls back only its own create effects: before registration it removes only the operation's own mkdtemp directory; after registration a failed `.fgos` strip unregisters and removes through the guarded non-destructive cleanup of §11 (never `--force`, never `rm -rf`) and rethrows the original cause unmasked. Rollback after a provisioning or setup failure belongs to Execution, which calls the guarded Worktree remove; releasing the runtime claim on create failure is Work/Execution policy. (override per RT2-F1) |
| G-034 | Carry §3/6/11 worktree/custody/recovery | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Khi tái dùng, di dời checkout mồ côi sang đường dẫn mới bằng `worktree move` (không hủy dữ liệu: move lỗi thì checkout cũ vẫn dùng được), hoặc `prune` đăng ký khi thư mục đã mất; thư mục placeholder phải xóa trước vì `worktree move` lồng vào thư mục đã tồn tại. |

| G-220 | Carry §5/6/10 foundation/recovery | V-ORDER/V-BORROW/V-CUSTODY/V-CRASH | Timeout 2000 ms và kill bằng SIGKILL, `maxBuffer` 64 KiB, env con bỏ `FGOS_INVOCATION_RECORD_PATH` để verb không ghi gì, truyền `--pid` của chính process gọi (Rust mặc định `getppid` nếu thiếu); cache: câu trả lời nhánh pid theo bộ env một lần cho cả process, câu trả lời env/registry theo (env, realpath của dir sâu nhất còn tồn tại cộng phần chưa tạo); lỗi không bao giờ được cache; facade chỉ trả shape `contract fgos.v1` hợp lệ, không có binary hay lỗi thì `WriterIdentityError` (exit 2) với mã `host-missing`, `timeout`, `host-version-mismatch`, `host-error`, `bad-output`, không bao giờ trả id đoán (G-157). |
| G-221 | Carry §5/6/10 foundation/recovery; old TTL/PID/unlink lock mechanism superseded by unchanged Holder-lock §5 | V-ORDER/V-BORROW/V-CUSTODY/V-CRASH | Thông báo chờ nêu người giữ, tuổi, ttl còn lại và gợi ý chính mình hay người khác chỉ ở mức chắc chắn có bằng chứng (token theo invocation/process, không suy 'cùng session id nghĩa là cùng lời gọi); nếu component thêm hàng đợi có thứ tự (ticket/FIFO) thì phải trả API vị trí hàng đợi và danh tính chi tiết, và không thay thế bảo đảm loại trừ. |
| G-222 | Carry §5/6/10 foundation/recovery | V-ORDER/V-BORROW/V-CUSTODY/V-CRASH | Component có điểm kiểm soát xác định (barrier / fault injection) cho mọi chứng minh race và crash: mất lock trước commit, chết ở từng rào git (G-111, G-112), đua so-sánh-rồi-xóa (G-124), append so với stage (G-120); không chứng minh crash/race bằng `sleep` hay heartbeat thời gian thực. |
| G-223 | Override per §16 G-166 / G-223 event-file; §16 G-223 PID-grant / truncation steps; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-TRUST/V-BORROW/V-ORDER | Effective rule: Event-file deletion only in authorized exact cutover grant after legacy import/verification; retain all other `.fgos` protections. Superseded by D-ADR0055 and Holder-lock borrow verification. Preserve ordering of **surviving** guards. |
| G-224 | Carry §5/7 hook guards | V-TRUST/V-BORROW/V-ORDER | Từ chối (fail-closed): reflog không đọc được, tip không đọc được, branch phân kỳ, blob không đọc được, `diff --cached` lỗi, lỗi kiểm tra file gốc, mutex mơ hồ, giao thức không hỗ trợ, `WriterIdentityError`. Cho qua (fail-open): HEAD tách rời (guard `fgw/*` và chỉ mục cũ không có gì để bảo vệ), beacon hỏng (chỉ gợi ý: cảnh báo và ghi đè), client convention thiếu (cảnh báo), cổng 'tại nhà' không khớp. Lỗi lạ không phải `WriterIdentityError` thì ném tiếp (commit bị chặn do crash hook). |
| G-225 | Carry §5/7 hook guards | V-TRUST/V-BORROW/V-ORDER | Component luôn ghi đường dẫn tuyệt đối của MAIN checkout, có test win32 thật, và `uninstall` không được xóa file đang được theo dõi (hoặc báo rõ). Điền chỗ trống, không bao giờ ghi đè `core.hooksPath` tùy chỉnh (`skippedExisting`). |
| G-226 | Carry §5/7 hook guards | V-TRUST/V-BORROW/V-ORDER | Component trả lời mọi câu hỏi của guard trong một lượt, có trần thời gian, và timeout thì fail-closed. |
| G-227 | Carry §1/3/9/11 consumer policy/guarded mutation | V-CONSUMER/V-CLEAN/V-PARITY | Component git chỉ cung cấp phần đọc diff; việc build/sinh nằm ngoài, và check nói rõ nó có đụng cây hay không. |
| G-228 | Carry §1/3/9/11 consumer policy/guarded mutation | V-CONSUMER/V-CLEAN/V-PARITY | `git mv`; nếu lỗi thì `renameSync` rồi `git add <mới> <cũ>`; nếu `git add` lỗi thì HOÀN NGUYÊN cả đường dẫn lẫn nội dung (khôi phục `raw` đã chụp trước khi sửa frontmatter), ném lỗi nói rõ registry CHƯA cập nhật để chạy lại được; chỉ ghi sự kiện registry sau khi git đã biết; path chứa ký tự shell được truyền bằng `execFileSync`, không qua shell. |
| G-229 | Carry §1/3/9/11 consumer policy/guarded mutation | V-CONSUMER/V-CLEAN/V-PARITY | Mọi thao tác checkout/reset/restore phá hủy: preflight các path bẩn, giữ đúng tài nguyên lock trong CÙNG giao dịch với kiểm tra, xác minh sha là commit, đọc trạng thái không phụ thuộc config người dùng, ghi nhận caller/ý định, tạo recovery artifact (snapshot hoặc patch) trước khi phá, và ghi provenance bền vững; git thô ngoài component phải bị phát hiện hoặc bị từ chối (G-154). |
| G-230 | Carry §12/13/15 consumer migration | V-PARITY/V-PACK/V-GATE | Component phải qua nguyên bộ test này không đổi (không chỉnh test để xanh): luồng add → dispatch → awaiting-approval → approve/return → delivered → cleanup; take/return/reject; xung đột branch; công việc của worker được runner commit; chạy từ linked worktree ghi vào main checkout. Không có hành vi git mới ngoài những G-id đã gắn. |
| G-231 | Carry §12/13/15 consumer migration | V-PARITY/V-PACK/V-GATE | Component cung cấp các fact git mà lớp điều phối đọc (HEAD, trạng thái dirty có phân loại, checkout đang giữ branch, baseline) với hợp đồng ổn định; thay đổi hình dạng fact là đổi hợp đồng cho mọi người tiêu thụ và cần cập nhật các test này cùng lúc. |
| G-232 | Carry §12/13/15 consumer migration | V-PARITY/V-PACK/V-GATE | Component không đổi cách các sự kiện git được ghi vào event log (tên trường, thời điểm) vì replay phụ thuộc chúng; mọi thay đổi định dạng sự kiện đi kèm cập nhật `replay`. |
| G-233 | Carry §12/13/15 consumer migration | V-PARITY/V-PACK/V-GATE | Mọi thay đổi chạm cài đặt/doctor phải theo cổng 'Install/setup/doctor' của AGENTS.md: giá trị mặc định, biến env hay phụ thuộc mới phải đăng ký vào `fgos setup` và `fgos doctor`; component git không đứng riêng. |
| G-234 | Override per §16 G-234; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-LAND/V-VERIFY/V-CRASH | Effective rule: Consumer owns Iron Law/approval; Git binds OIDs/target/evidence. |

The Inspect driver exposes `hash_object(repo, ObjectType, bytes)` for blob, tree and commit identities. It runs `git hash-object -t <type> --stdin` through the existing read-only command door, without `-w`, installing no object and borrowing no publication authority.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.text:
| Lesson | Disposition / owning contract | Vector | Frozen obligation carried (legacy mechanism subject to disposition) |
|---|---|---|---|
| G-001 | Override per §16 G-001 / G-183; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Effective rule: Two named env contexts, one backend owner: scrubbed runner; validated hook-index context. |
| G-002 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Gitdir của worktree chỉ lấy từ con trỏ `worktrees/<name>/gitdir` của repo chính, khớp theo realpath với worktree; không bao giờ đọc từ `.git` của worktree. `repoRoot` phải là main checkout thật (cha của common-dir bằng chính nó); linked worktree, worktree không thuộc repo, hoặc thiếu `repoRoot` đều bị từ chối bằng `untrusted-worktree`. |
| G-003 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi git của runner mang `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. |
| G-004 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | `core.hooksPath` tương đối được resolve theo main checkout; đường dẫn tuyệt đối hoặc `~` giữ nguyên. Khi cài đặt, luôn ghi `core.hooksPath` tuyệt đối trỏ vào `.githooks` của main checkout. |
| G-005 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi merge của runner chạy với `rerere.enabled=false` và `merge.autoStash=false`. |
| G-006 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Dùng danh tính của chính repo; chỉ khi một trường chưa đặt mới dùng `fgOS runner <runner@fgos.local>`. |
| G-007 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Resolve base bằng `rev-parse -q --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`; kết quả null nghĩa là 'không trỏ tới commit nào' và bị từ chối trước khi có run. |
| G-008 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Lệnh con kết thúc theo sự kiện thoát của chính child trực tiếp, và timeout phải thực sự chặn được thao tác kể cả khi hậu duệ giữ descriptor. Rust cần quyết định có leo thang từ SIGTERM lên kill cả nhóm process hay không (code cũ không làm). |
| G-009 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lỗi git mang `stderr` và exit status qua mọi ranh giới trừu tượng (typed error/outcome); lỗi do tràn buffer thành lỗi nghiệp vụ có hướng dẫn ('sync/rebase it'); lỗi trong các hàm đọc ánh xạ về một mã validation thống nhất; probe cố ý fail-open thì nuốt stderr; nhánh fail-closed giữ nguyên nguyên nhân gốc. |
| G-010 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi nơi đọc danh sách path của git đều dùng `-z` và tách theo NUL: path đúng bằng byte git đặt tên, không trim; trong `status --porcelain=v1 -z` bản ghi có R hoặc C ở bất kỳ cột nào đọc thêm trường kế làm path thứ hai và trả cả hai nửa, khử trùng; `diff --name-status -z` đọc R/C thành hai path; bỏ dấu `/` cuối của thư mục untracked bị gộp; bỏ phần tử rỗng. |
| G-011 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Bộ đọc danh sách path có trần output 64 MiB; diff đầy đủ cho review có trần 50 MiB; hook đọc blob với buffer 200 MB; vượt trần phải báo thành lỗi chẩn đoán được, không phải ENOBUFS thô. Component Rust phải truyền dữ liệu theo luồng hoặc có ngưỡng tường minh tương đương. |
| G-012 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi `diff` trả danh sách path đều truyền `--no-relative`. |
| G-013 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Mọi lời gọi `status` đọc danh sách truyền tường minh `--untracked-files=all` (hoặc `normal` khi chỉ cần biết có bẩn hay không), bất kể config người dùng. |
| G-014 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Danh sách staged và changed-file dùng `--no-renames` để mỗi nửa được xét riêng; ngoại lệ duy nhất là `branchContentMismatch`, nơi chỉ cần tên mới nên bật detect rename. |
| G-015 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Pathspec luôn là literal: `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1` cùng `--pathspec-from-file=-` phân tách NUL trên stdin (không giới hạn độ dài), hoặc `--literal-pathspecs`. |
| G-016 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | So sánh path checkout sau `realpath.native`, bỏ tiền tố mở rộng, chuẩn hóa dấu phân cách, không phân biệt hoa/thường trên win32; chạy executable theo ngữ nghĩa từng nền tảng (shell cho `.cmd`); kiểm tra liveness và định danh process đi qua một adapter nền tảng. |
| G-017 | Carry §2/7 driver, parsing, trust | V-TRUST/V-SCOPE/V-PARITY | Component mới dùng `-z` ở mọi nơi, kể cả `worktree list --porcelain -z`, để không có ngoại lệ nào phụ thuộc vào việc 'chỉ test rỗng'. |
| G-018 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Trunk là đích của `origin/HEAD`, nếu không có thì `main`/`master` cục bộ, cuối cùng mới là chữ `main`; tương tự bước workflow `integrate` phải nhận đích tường minh. Không nơi nào được viết cứng `main`; còn cần quyết định các nhãn `main` trong approve/catchup là chủ ý hay sót. |
| G-019 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Main checkout được nhận diện theo cấu trúc (git-dir bằng common-dir, toplevel), không theo registry. Đường dẫn không phải repo git coi là main (fail open, chưa có test). Root là tham số tường minh (`--dir`), cwd chỉ là ngữ cảnh. Verb ghi từ worktree không nối với store sống bị từ chối trừ khi có `--dir` trỏ main. |
| G-020 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Hàm ancestry ba giá trị: exit 1 nghĩa là không, mọi mã khác ném lỗi (`MergeError`). Cả sync, catchup, approve và cleanup dùng chung hàm này. |
| G-021 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | `isCheckoutDirty` fail-closed (lỗi nghĩa là bẩn) và loại `:!.fgos`; `checkoutDirtyPaths` (chỉ liệt kê) fail-open ra danh sách rỗng; độ bẩn khi resync được đánh giá so với commit đồng bộ gần nhất, không so với HEAD hiện tại. |
| G-022 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Parse stanza (`worktree `, `branch `, dòng trống) và trả realpath của checkout đang giữ branch, hoặc null. |
| G-023 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Tính `rev-parse --show-prefix` (chỉ cắt dấu xuống dòng vì tên có thể bắt đầu hay kết thúc bằng khoảng trắng) và so `.fgos` với tiền tố đó. |
| G-024 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Đọc tip của ref có tên bằng `rev-parse <ref>` từ repo root, không phải HEAD của worktree nào đó. |
| G-025 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Điểm đồng bộ của worktree là mục reflog mới nhất của chính HEAD (`reflog show HEAD -n 1`), không phải `rev-parse HEAD`; reflog hoặc tip không đọc được thì fail closed. |
| G-026 | Carry §2/3/7 topology, explicit facts | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Tìm MERGE_HEAD bằng `rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD` (đúng cả trong linked worktree). Ba luật sở hữu (sync unit, approve/merge, hook) được giữ riêng ở các mục về sync và land. |
| G-027 | Override per §16 G-027; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-TRUST/V-LAND | Effective rule: Work owns claim reclaim **policy**. Git supplies facts (status, mtimes, branch tips) only. Do not claim reclaim in a Git facts row. |
| G-028 | Carry §3/6/11 worktree/custody/recovery | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Tái dùng branch `fgw/<id>` đã có (không bao giờ `-b` lại) và luôn cấp thư mục `mkdtemp` mới; nếu branch chưa tồn tại thì `-b <branch> <path> <baseRef>`; đường dẫn trả về là realpath. Phục hồi sau crash phải idempotent và có kết quả blocked được phân loại, không crash lặp lại. |
| G-029 | Partial retirement: event-file workaround gone; provisioning/non-event worktree rules retained §3/11 | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Sau mỗi checkout (và sau mọi `reset --hard`) xóa hẳn `.fgos/` khỏi worktree của worker. Nhánh worker không bao giờ tạo hay chở trạng thái control-plane. Đường workflow `createWorkflowWorktree` hiện không strip (xác minh `integrate.mjs:33-63`), component mới phải áp dụng cho mọi cửa tạo worktree. |
| G-030 | Override per §16 G-030 / G-031; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: **Execution**, after `worktree-create` returns, outside every Git lock. Git does not spawn `npm` or setup commands. |
| G-031 | Override per §16 G-030 / G-031; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: **Execution**, after `worktree-create` returns, outside every Git lock. Git does not spawn `npm` or setup commands. |
| G-032 | Override per §16 G-032; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: Git worktree-create ends at registration and the worker `.fgos` strip, then returns; it takes no `beforeProvision` callback. Execution provisions dependencies and runs setup after create returns, outside every Git lock (§1, G-030/G-031). Retained lesson: a lock is held only for the narrow Git metadata mutation, and nothing holds main while provisioning runs. (override per RT2-F1) |
| G-033 | Override per §16 G-033; frozen text stays in the catalogue, superseded mechanics are not carried | V-CUSTODY/V-CLEAN/V-CRASH | Effective rule: Git rolls back only its own create effects: before registration it removes only the operation's own mkdtemp directory; after registration a failed `.fgos` strip unregisters and removes through the guarded non-destructive cleanup of §11 (never `--force`, never `rm -rf`) and rethrows the original cause unmasked. Rollback after a provisioning or setup failure belongs to Execution, which calls the guarded Worktree remove; releasing the runtime claim on create failure is Work/Execution policy. (override per RT2-F1) |

docs/platform/git/spec.md.sample: Phase 06 unit 10 recovery review notes
ancestry: Appendix A. Per-row catalogue disposition G-001..G-234
docs/platform/git/spec.md.text: ### Phase 06 unit 10 recovery review notes
docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
### Phase 06 unit 10 recovery review notes

Native quarantine compares the moved file's device/inode after rename. A
substitution is restored with a no-overwrite hard link; if the original path
is occupied, both paths are preserved and the inspection report identifies
the retained quarantine path. This does not claim successful repair.

Config recovery intentionally preserves config.lock if a writer dies after
writing bytes but before appending the updated NativeLockOwned capture:
intent-time empty-file evidence no longer matches. Inspect the retained WAL,
config.lock and local config before manual repair; a new config operation
cannot bypass this unresolved evidence. Hooks removal uses --fixed-value,
which Git supports since 2.30, below the declared 2.53.0 floor.

Hooks provenance uses an optional WAL ConfigChange configSequence, assigned
under repo-config authority from retained config history. Directory mtimes do
not establish ownership order. Historical digests omit this field; ambiguous
latest historical provenance refuses ownership. Config provenance chains remain
retained and inspection remains bounded by 100,000 chains (L4).

Phase 06 unit 11 adds `packages/git/rust/tests/recovery_matrix.rs`: all twelve
Recovery payload kinds run through their real operation ports and receive
SIGKILL immediately after the directory fsync installing Intent. Each kind is
run twice, with Recovery first and with the owning recovery port first. The
matrix checks pending discovery, kind/intent inspection, the terminal
`abandonedBeforeAttempt` outcome, and request-digest/outcome retention after
compaction. Restore uses its acknowledgement; Land and Publication use their
own cleanup; other uncompacted cases use the existing WAL compactor while
holding the owning resource and reading real refs. This establishes the
pre-attempt row for every kind, not every internal or post-effect crash point.
Compacted Recovery returns the retained Outcome; a typed owning port such as
Sync may reconstruct a different response shape with the same terminal state.

Acceptance remains incomplete. The borrowed spawn port still lacks a
pre-execution identity callback; index ownership's production producer remains
unresolved (the fixture recorder is crate-private and test-only). Process
identity recorded before exec is necessary but does not alone attribute an
inode: a foreign Git can create index.lock after the absence check and before
the stopped child resumes. No such residue may be adopted merely because the
recorded child later died. Native repair callers must not be wired until both
the spawn boundary and artifact attribution are established.

docs/platform/git/spec.md.sectionText:
### Cooperative termination host acceptance

Real Git read-tree/index.lock cleanup tests live in the Git crate’s
`borrow_deadline` suite; holder-lock retains generic cooperative/forced deadline
coverage. Readiness budgets allow five seconds for the generic handler and eight
seconds for Git’s filter (ten-second Git deadline).
The Linux namespace-init case is explicitly ignored in ordinary runs. An eligible
host must run this exact merge gate, which fails if its bwrap probe fails:

```sh
cargo test -p fgos-git --test borrow_deadline real_read_tree_deadline_as_namespace_init_cleans_its_native_lock -- --exact --ignored --nocapture
```

An ignored test is not passing acceptance evidence. Full `npm test` and E3 remain
separate required host merge gates.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 1. Purpose
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 1. Purpose
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 1. Purpose
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 1. Purpose

Holder-lock answers one question for every cold lock in fgOS: who holds this resource right now, as the kernel sees it. A lock is a kernel lock on an open file description. The kernel releases it when every process holding a copy of that description has died, so no decision anywhere in the component is derived from a pid, a TTL, a start time or an mtime. The one pid the component reads is the locker identity the kernel itself stamps on a lock record (`flock` stores the calling process's pid on the description's lock); it is compared only against this live process's own pid, never used to infer liveness or ownership of a record.

Every caller (the Node facade, a Rust crate, a git hook) goes through one port with one set of operations. Each operating system has one driver behind the port, and the port reports the guarantee level that driver gives on the filesystem the lock files live on. Nothing in the public interface is POSIX-only: a caller never sees a file descriptor or a handle of the operating system.

The component owns the cold locks, the main checkout mutex, the merge slot and `worktree-admin` (sections 14 and 16). The state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`) is built on the same facade for its cleanup lock but is implemented by the state store, not by this component (section 15).

Each operating system has one driver behind the port, and the port reports the guarantee level that driver gives on the filesystem the lock files live on. docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 2. Ownership boundary
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 2. Ownership boundary
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 2. Ownership boundary

| Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|
| The port: `acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee` ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/holder-lock.port.v1.json)) | Writer identity (Session Identity) |
| Which process holds which resource, as the kernel reports it | Taking a lock away from a live holder (there is no such path; a hung live holder is stopped by a person, `fgos lock fence`, section 17) |
| Lock order inside one `LockScope` and the description rules (section 5) | Liveness judgment of a process tuple (process facts) |
| The lock registry: every lock's name, kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence ([registry](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json)) | The attempt lock's lifecycle (run supervisor) and the containment port (process control) |
| The single state-root resolution and `lockRoot` (section 11) | The meaning of a lock's contents (a lock file is never read for data) |
| The internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd`, `state-root`, `process-observe`, `quiesce-scan`, `lock-borrow-vectors` (section 10) | Any verb a person calls |
| The cutover fences for the retired lock shapes and the stop-everything check (section 12) | Deciding when a workspace is cut over (a person, through `fgos doctor --fix`) |

There is one implementation of the primitive, the Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock`, which calls `flock` in process. Node cannot call `flock`, so the Node facade in `src/holder-lock/` opens the lock file itself and hands the description to the internal route `fgos internal lock-fd`, which locks the inherited description and exits. The lock stays with the description Node owns; the helper is never the owner. Rust and Node lock the same file with the same primitive, so a Rust writer and a Node writer exclude each other with no second protocol.

Depends on `fgos-process` (facts and control) and on the kernel. The component-boundary entry is [Holder-lock (L1)](../component-boundary.md#4-current-high-level-components).

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 3. The port
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 3. The port
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 3. The port

Operations, as the contract states them:

| Operation | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `acquire(resource, mode: EX \| SH, wait: try \| ms N, killWaitMs)` | Hold the lock. Returns `acquired` with an opaque handle, `held` (reason `kernel-lock-held` or `predecessor-domain-not-empty`, with the holders when they are listable), `timeout` with the milliseconds waited, or `unavailable` (`unsupported-platform`, `unsupported-filesystem`, `host-version-mismatch`, `io-error`). `acquired` is returned only when both hold: the kernel lock is held and the predecessor domain recorded next to the lock file is empty (section 8). A free kernel lock alone is not proof |
| `clear_domain(handle)` | Recorded handoff: while holding an idle exclusive acquired handle, observe its own domain empty without killing, then remove the unchanged predecessor record. Node: `handle.clearDomain()`. Execution attaches `custody-handoff-not-recorded` to its returned settled result if this fails, retaining its original outcome. Failure preserves the record; a replaced resource refuses |
| `release(handle)` | Close every copy of the description the handle owns. The holder releases only after its own domain is empty (section 8, step 0) |
| `run_borrowed(handle, spec)` | The only way a child command (a git commit of a checkpoint or merge) runs with the holder's authority. The description goes to exactly one child through an explicit fd mapping (slot 3 by default, env `FGOS_LOCK_FD=<name>:3`). When the command is git, `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` is prepended. After the child exits the leftovers in the domain are killed and the call waits for the domain to be empty before it returns `{exit, signal, leftoversKilled}` |
| `run_borrowed_io(handle, spec, io)` | Synchronous member of `run_borrowed` with binary stdin, bounded captured stdout/stderr and an absolute monotonic deadline; returns captured bytes and the ordinary borrow outcome after cleanup. Unix only; Windows refuses `borrow-io-unsupported` before spawn and retains existing `run_borrowed` behavior |
| `probe(resource)` | One non-blocking `LOCK_SH` attempt on a fresh description, dropped at once; answers `free` or `held` and never obstructs a holder. Used by the adopt scan, the resume guard and reconcile |
| `holders(resource)` | Diagnostic list `[{pid, startTime, cmdline}]` of every process holding a description of the lock file, or `unlistable` with a reason. Linux reads `/proc/*/fdinfo/*` for a `lock:` line on the file's inode; macOS and Windows report `unlistable` |
| `guarantee(path)` | `{driver, exclusion, borrow, holders, platform, notes}` for the directory the lock files live in. The levels are `kernel`, `kernel-unmeasured`, `job-scoped`, `unsupported`, `none` |

Invariants of every result:

- `held` and `timeout` never leave a description open: the lock is released before the result is returned, and `predecessor-domain-not-empty` is returned after the kernel lock was released again.
- No result of any operation is derived from a pid, a TTL or an mtime.
- A handle is opaque. The fd lives only inside the driver; `run_borrowed` is the one place that maps it into a child.

The lock file of a resource is created once and never removed while the resource lives. A lock whose resource is a run (`attempt`, `advance`, `recovery`) lives in the run directory and goes away with the run; the inode check in section 5 makes that safe.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 4. Drivers and guarantee levels
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 4. Drivers and guarantee levels
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 4. Drivers and guarantee levels
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 4. Drivers and guarantee levels

Each platform runs at the highest level it has, and the level is said out loud: `fgos doctor` prints it (`lock-kernel-semantics`), `fgctl` refuses to activate a release whose level is red (section 13). No platform falls back to the retired TTL locks.

| Driver | Exclusion | Borrow (`run_borrowed`) | Holders | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Linux `flock`, local filesystem | `kernel` (measured) | `kernel`: the description is passed to exactly one child at spawn; the git hook checks it by try-lock on the inherited description | `kernel` (fdinfo) | The first driver |
| macOS `flock` | `kernel` (measured 2026-10-16 on macOS 26.6 arm64: the lock is released on SIGKILL, an inherited fd keeps the lock after the parent dies, the borrow path never shows the lock free while git or its child is alive) | `kernel`, as Linux | `unsupported` (`unlistable`) | Enabled at once; still gated at activation by the borrow vectors and the semantics probe. Containment on macOS is best-effort (a `setsid` + double-fork escapee survives a group kill) and is reported in `notes`, not as a level |
| Windows `LockFileEx` (`lockfileex`), local volume | `kernel` (measured: released 0.1 ms after `TerminateProcess`) | `job-scoped`: the locking process keeps the lock and runs the child inside a named `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` job (section 8.1); a handle is never inherited | `unsupported` (`unlistable`: Win32 lists no byte-range lock holders) | Doctor and `fgctl` print the exclusion level, `kernel`; `job-scoped` is the borrow level. A remote volume (`GetDriveTypeW == DRIVE_REMOTE`) gives `none` and `unsupported-filesystem`. Node reaches the lock through one `lock-hold` helper per held lock (section 8.1) |
| NFS, SMB, CIFS | `none` | `none` | `none` | The driver refuses with a named error (`unsupported-filesystem`); doctor fails by name |

The guarantee is asked once per lock directory and per process. A directory whose exclusion level is `none`, or a platform with no driver (doctor and `fgctl` fail it by name), makes every `acquire` of the facade fail with the named error `lock-driver-unavailable`.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: 5. Description rules
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 5. Description rules
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 5. Description rules
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 5. Description rules

The boundary between right and wrong moved from "who is alive" to "who holds a copy of the description". These rules are mandatory and have tests:

1. The lock description is always `FD_CLOEXEC`. The one moment it is not is inside exactly one spawn that borrows it, through an explicit fd mapping (Node: a `stdio` slot; Rust: `dup2` in `pre_exec`).
2. The receiver (inherited fd 3, or `SCM_RIGHTS` with `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC`) sets `FD_CLOEXEC` before any other syscall.
3. Reason, with evidence: Node opens with `O_CLOEXEC`, but Rust's `std::process::Command` inherits every fd above 2 that is not `CLOEXEC`. Every Rust route that receives a description has a leak test: after the child ran, `/proc/<child>/fd` and a grandchild's fd table do not contain the lock inode.
4. After acquire, `fstat(fd).ino` must equal `stat(path).ino`; otherwise close and retry. This is what lets a lock file be removed with its resource.
5. The lock file is opened `O_RDWR` (NFSv4 and BSD refuse an exclusive lock on a read-only fd).
6. Borrowing is a strong right and is close-only: any copy that calls `LOCK_UN` releases the shared lock, so owner and borrower only `close`; no library guard that unlocks on drop is used.
7. The doctor check `lock-holders` reports every holder that is not an fgOS process, so a violation shows up at once. The bwrap monitor process of an attempt whose supervisor or gate holds the lock is a member, not a stranger.
8. The borrow vectors are mandatory and there is no run-time switch that disables borrowing (such a switch would block fgOS's own commits and trip after every release). The vectors run in a throwaway repository with real git: a git alias that starts a background shell process, a clean/smudge filter that starts a background process, a hook that starts a background process, and `gc.auto=1` with enough loose objects; each asserts the lock is free as soon as git has exited and the owner closed its description, plus the sibling check (a process with the same `FGOS_LOCK_FD` value that opened the file itself is not a borrower). A red vector is a doctor FAIL (`lock-borrow-vectors`) and `fgctl` refuses to activate.

The borrower test used by a hook has three conditions, all required: `FGOS_LOCK_FD` names exactly the slot, `fstat(slot)` has the same `dev:ino` as the lock file, and `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` on the slot succeeds (a description that already holds the lock succeeds; a sibling that opened the file itself fails). Missing any one, the hook tries the lock once on a description of its own and never claims to be a borrower. The worker base env of a dispatch scrubs `FGOS_LOCK_FD` and `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`; a leaked variable is useless without the description.

Node synchronous `runBorrowed` accepts a positive `spec.maxOutputBytes` per captured stream (default 16 MiB); commit children request 64 MiB. Both transports refuse overflow rather than returning truncated output. The fd transport also completes leftover cleanup before reporting capture failure.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.title: Explicit I/O borrowing
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: Explicit I/O borrowing
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ### Explicit I/O borrowing
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
### Explicit I/O borrowing

**Extended 2026-10-18 for Git Publication: run_borrowed with explicit input, bounded capture and deadline; same lifecycle as run_borrowed.** `run_borrowed_io(&Handle, &BorrowSpec, &BorrowIo)` borrows an exclusive opaque handle for the entire synchronous call. `BorrowIo` supplies binary stdin (EOF after its last byte), independent stdout/stderr byte ceilings and an absolute monotonic `Instant` deadline. It supersedes `BorrowSpec.stdio`. The result contains only captured byte vectors and the ordinary exit/signal/leftover outcome, never a running child, pipe, fd or owning handle. Input and both captures progress concurrently with nonblocking parent pipe ends, so a child that ignores stdin cannot prevent deadline enforcement.

Unix uses the existing `run_borrowed` spawn door and explicit slot-3 mapping, environment annotation, git auto-gc/maintenance disabling, driver preparation and release rule. It introduces no additional containment backend or suspended-start barrier. Predecessor handling stays unchanged: Linux borrows declare no new predecessor record and clean up the borrowed child's process group and descendants; macOS uses the child's process group. Git Publication disables hooks in its own driver before calling this port, as Git spec §10 rule 4a requires.

Exceeding either byte ceiling returns `borrow-output-limit: stdout|stderr`; reaching the deadline returns `borrow-deadline: terminated|killed-after-grace` (`BorrowError::Deadline { termination }`). On either refusal, or an I/O failure (`borrow-io-failed`), SIGTERM is sent to the child group while the root remains unreaped; the handle's internal `terminate_grace_ms` field (beside `kill_wait_ms`, default 3000 ms, no new config key) bounds the grace. If the root exits during grace the deadline outcome is `terminated`; otherwise SIGKILL yields `killed-after-grace`. The root is then waited without reaping, the existing borrow domain's leftovers are ended, and the root is reaped before returning. The handle remains owned by the caller throughout. Remaining output is drained after normal root exit and leftover cleanup. As with `run_borrowed`, failure to end leftovers takes precedence and returns `borrow-leftover-not-killed`; this is never a successful empty-domain claim. Windows refuses this new form with `borrow-io-unsupported` before any child is started; its existing job-backed `run_borrowed` is unchanged.

Clarified 2026-10-18 (refined): every acquire opens its own description. Outside a borrow, only the holder and its direct children between fork and exec can hold that description; it is close-on-exec everywhere else. On Linux drain, holders in the borrowed child's process group or descended from it are killed. A direct child outside the borrow group is protected as a pre-exec child while its locked copies retain `FD_CLOEXEC`: wait bounded by `killWaitMs` and re-check, never kill it. A tagged locked copy without `FD_CLOEXEC` proves explicit borrow mapping, so an adopted direct child with such a copy remains a borrower escapee and is killed. Unreadable descriptor flags never supply that authority. Any other holder of the description can only be an escaped descendant of a borrowed child, is inside the borrow's authority, and is killed, then drained and verified. Signals pin and re-check process identity. The Node fd facade routes drain through the Rust `lock-fd --drain-child` helper, passing the held description explicitly; the helper excludes itself and its parent (the holder) and applies this same rule. Unix borrowed children remain leaders of their own process groups. Non-spawning `validate_quiescent(&Handle)` has no borrow kill authority: it waits bounded and refuses unresolved holders before Publication writes Intent or supersession. A timeout or unprovable drain retains the held handle and exclusion; it never claims empty.

Clarified 2026-10-19: a narrowed per-spawn `Reach::Since` pass assumes that copies are inherited by fork, ordinary cyclic PID allocation is used (no privileged `clone3(set_tid)` or `ns_last_pid` override), and allocation stays below 4,000,000 PIDs/s inside the `pid_max / 4,000,000` window. An old or unreadable allocation mark falls back to start-time filtering over the process table. Descriptor transfers by `SCM_RIGHTS` or `pidfd_getfd` to pre-existing processes are outside that narrowed candidate set. The floor lags by one successful proof: proof N advances it only to the start of proof N-1, so a fork in flight at proof N remains eligible at N+1. Failed and out-of-order proofs do not advance it.

Clarified 2026-10-19 (supersedes the same-day full-scan admission/borrow-return rule): the narrowed `Reach::Since` pass is the only drain of a borrow return and of non-spawning `validate_quiescent`; it kills fork-inherited escapees promptly and never decides that the lock is free. The lock-freeing decision is made once, at exclusive Linux release. Capture the original description's stat key, exact fdinfo `major:minor:inode` token and the holder's proc-mount pid; reject a mismatched PID namespace. Open an independent, noncreating description through `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` and verify its inode before closing the original, so an unlinked/replaced pathname cannot redirect the later probe. This is an open, never a dup: the independent description is initially unlocked and does not retain the original flock.

After close, `/proc/locks` is read to EOF on one open seq_file and supplies positive evidence: a FLOCK record with the exact token and this process as locker proves a leaked copy. **An absent record does not prove release.** Kernel `seq_read_iter` can return a short page even into a larger userspace buffer, so the reader continues until EOF. This read is not an atomic snapshot and concurrent lock changes may affect it. With no matching record, try `LOCK_SH | LOCK_NB` on the independent inode-checked description: success proves the old EX description gone; close the probe immediately and return released. This brief SH hold can cause a concurrent exclusive `Wait::Try` acquirer to report held. The coordinator accepted this contention window after the short-read reproduction on 2026-10-19.

A positive tagged record, blocked probe or any uncertainty enters the full tagged descriptor scan. Holders of this inode whose FLOCK record stamps this process are signalled by an identity captured before scanning their descriptors and pinned again at signal time, except direct pre-exec children whose locked copies retain `FD_CLOEXEC` (waited, never killed); a tagged non-CLOEXEC copy identifies an adopted borrower and is settled through this same door. A live own handle, or a positive record of a later acquirer, proves the old EX description gone by exclusivity and spares that acquirer and its borrowers. Recheck own handles before each signal; no kcmp is necessary once the own-handle proof holds. An empty scan alone does not prove release across an in-flight fork: repeat table/probe/scan until positively proven or `killWaitMs` passes, returning `lock-release-stuck` with killed count and remaining pids. A dropped handle runs the same settle; `release` returns its outcome. Descriptor transfer to a pre-existing process is found at release, not borrow return: such a recipient runs until release, at most the length of the hold. Shared handles close directly. The Node facade passes its guarantee observation as `--reach-floor-ticks` to `lock-fd --drain-child`; missing or future history refuses rather than scanning everyone on each spawn.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: Node handover trust boundary (2026-10-19 review)
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ### Node handover trust boundary (2026-10-19 review)
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
### Node handover trust boundary (2026-10-19 review)

The opaque addon handover protects acquired handles from request-data forgery; it is not an isolation boundary against arbitrary code already executing inside the Node process. The first-caller registration capability is per Node worker thread. Code that loads the native addon before the trusted facade can consume that capability and deny facade startup (fail closed). A hostile module or worker thread therefore requires process isolation; possession of request data, a path or an fd number never grants a holder handle. Native borrowed copies remain close-only and are drained before the facade borrow guard releases. The Node acquisition path retains the actual `reachFloorTicks` observation returned by the existing Rust `lock-fd --guarantee` call **before** opening its acquired description. A cached observation remains an older, conservative bound; it is never refreshed onto an existing handle. The private handle map carries that bound and the live async sibling borrow roots into the opaque native loan. Mint refuses while an async drain snapshot is active, so the snapshot cannot miss a new native child. Rust retains the observed boot ticks with PID-allocation narrowing disabled across the process boundary, then applies its ordinary lagged successful-proof rule within the loan; no handover-time timestamp or `Reach::Everyone` per child substitutes for provenance. A missing/unreadable floor or a future floor refuses handover (`lock-reach-history-missing`, `lock-reach-clock-unreadable`, `lock-reach-floor-invalid`); an older host must be rebuilt with the matching facade/addon. This path establishes the bound at acquisition, so it does not need to assert an unproven alone-state at handover.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 6. Kinds
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 6. Kinds

| Kind | Mechanism | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `mutex` | Kernel lock, held briefly | sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, provider account, provider state, main checkout, `worktree-admin`, merge slot, `event-seal` (58), `event-append` (70); later observe, activation, install |
| `lease` | Kernel lock, held for the length of a long job; may be handed to a gate | gateway, runner, dispatch cwd, full-suite; later the attempt lock, whose file lives in the run directory |
| `hot-mutex` | link-created record for the fast path; the row's kernel lock (`<resource>.reclaim.lock`) only serialises cleanup of a dead holder's record (section 15) | `state`, `porting-events` |
| `beacon` | Not a lock | the main-checkout activity file (read by the hook only when the commit is not a borrower, section 14) |

Run control is not a kind: its ledger and CAS stay as they are, with no garbage collection; real exclusion of an attempt is the attempt lock.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sample: 7. Registry
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ## 7. Registry
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 7. Registry

[`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json) (schema [`lock-registry.schema.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.schema.v1.json)) is the only list of which locks exist, in which order they may be taken, and which fence the cutover places for them. Rust and Node read the same file; the Node facade resolves the path templates (`<fgosDir>`, `<lockRoot>`, `<runDir>`, `<workflowRunDir>`).

`<eventOpenRoot>` is the resolved Git common directory plus `fgos/events`; Event Store owns its two repo mutexes, `event-seal` (58) and `event-append` (70), at `<eventOpenRoot>/locks/<name>.lock`. Both have no legacy shape/path and fence `none`. Only Rust resolves this template; Node refuses these rows with `lock-not-node-owned`. Append is released before Git calls; seal is never taken inside the Work gate.

One row per lock: `name`, `kind`, `scope` (`repo`, `machine`, `run`), `rank`, `v3Path`, `v1Shape` (`file-link`, `file-wx`, `ledger-dir`, `file-by-cwd`), `v1Path`, `fence` (`tombstone`, `blocking-generation`, `none`), `owner` (the track that cuts it over: `4.2`, `4.3`, `4.4`, `6.2`, `event-store`), and notes. A row owned by this track must carry a fence, a legacy shape, a legacy path and a new path.

Ranks (a scope may only take a lock of a higher rank than every lock it holds):

| Rank | Locks | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | `runner`, `gateway` | lease |
| 15 | `attempt` | lease |
| 20 | `merge-slot` | mutex |
| 30 | `dispatch-cwd` | lease |
| 40 | `worktree-admin` | mutex |
| 50 | `main-checkout` | mutex |
| 55 | git's own `index.lock`: outside fgOS, no row; the hook tries rank 50 once | — |
| 58 | `event-seal` | mutex |
| 60 | `state`, `porting-events` | hot-mutex |
| 70 | `event-append` | mutex |
| 80 | leaves: `sessions`, `advance`, `reconcile`, `recovery`, `full-suite`, `provider-account`, `provider-state`, `observe`, `activation`, `install` | mutex, lease |

The ranks 58 (`event-seal`) and 70 (`event-append`) above are declared by the signed [Event Store spec §4](../event-store/spec.md#4-layering-and-locks), D-ADR0055; implementation has not started. They are planned additions to the shipped registry, which currently declares neither rank nor lock. They do not claim a registered kind, path or cutover. The design permits `state` (60) → `event-append` (70) and forbids seal/sync under `state`; registry and implementation must land together under the Event Store proof gates.

Locks cut over by this track: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `advance`, `reconcile`, `recovery`, `full-suite`, `provider-account`, `provider-state`, `dispatch-cwd`. Their new files live under `<fgosDir>/locks/` (repo scope), `<lockRoot>/` (machine scope) or a `locks/` directory inside the run (`<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), so a run's new lock never lands on the tombstone of its legacy path. The dispatch cwd lock is keyed by the directory's identity after `realpath` (`<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`), so a worktree reached through a symlink is the same lock. The npm package and the staged legacy-node payload ship the registry file, because every lock of this track resolves through it. The dispatch cwd lock keeps the `fgosDir` scope; a machine-wide cwd lock is a separate item, opened only when two workspaces share one cwd for real.

Locks cut over by the Rust-callers track (registry owner `4.4`), all leaves of rank 80, all mutex, all fenced by a tombstone:

| Lock | Scope | New path | Legacy path (becomes a tombstone directory) | Caller |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `activation` | repo | `<fgosDir>/locks/activation-v2.lock` | `.fgos/installation/activation.lock` and `.fgos/locks/activation.lock` | `fgctl` init, upgrade, repair |
| `install` | machine | `<lockRoot>/install.lock` (`<stateRoot>/locks/install.lock`) | `<stateRoot>/install.lock` | `fgctl` release store |
| `observe` | repo | `<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock` | `.fgos/observe/.lock` | Observe store (`fgos metrics`, `fgos friction`) |

Git adds `repo-config`, a repo mutex at rank 80, `<fgosDir>/locks/repo-config.lock`, with no legacy path. It serializes the local fetch-mapping writer; Git's native `config.lock` also excludes ordinary Git config writers.

The observe lock waits at most 5 s, has no TTL, and the shard snapshot is written under it. The activation and install locks are held by `fgctl` through the crate it links; a holder that is killed leaves the lock free at once. Until the main-checkout lock is cut over, `fgctl` checks the main checkout with `probe` (shared, non-blocking, never held) plus the v1 read, and reads a directory at `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` (a tombstone) as "moved".

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
## 8. The predecessor domain rule

Measured on Windows: a lock bound to a process is released the moment that process dies, while the job that kills its children does so asynchronously, so for a few milliseconds the lock reads free while a borrowed git may still be writing. Linux and macOS have no such gap on the borrow path (git itself holds a copy of the description), but the rule is part of the port from the first driver so no driver can be written without it ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/predecessor.v1.json)).

0. **Release rule (custody extension, 2026-10-18).** The holder clears only its own unchanged predecessor record with `clear_domain(handle)` after observing its domain empty, while still holding exclusion, then closes. Execution does this after the runner commit receipt and persisted handoff. An absent record means a recorded handoff or that no producer ran. An unknown launch or unproven domain leaves the record for successor admission. `clear_domain` never kills a domain. **Limitation (owner decision 2026-10-19):** for a best-effort domain kind (`linux-pgroup`, `macos-tree`) "observed empty" sees the process group or tree only, so a `setsid` or double-fork escapee is not seen and a recorded handoff over such a domain does not cover it; admission after a controller death still refuses these kinds. On supervised Linux the attempt gate is a subreaper and kills adopted escapees before the receipt, so the exposure is unconfined Linux and macOS. Revisit when containment drivers give those platforms a provable domain.

   **Borrow cleanup.** Cleanup covers the borrowed child's process group, descendants and escaped description holders under §5's refined 2026-10-18 rule. Only direct pre-exec children of the holder outside the borrow group are waited, never killed. Hook-enabled borrows (including checkpoint and merge commits) still kill setsid/double-fork escapees holding the description; ancestry loss does not spare an escapee. A holder releases only after `run_borrowed` has waited for the child, killed leftovers in its authority, drained and verified empty. A non-empty predecessor domain found after the next holder took the lock means the previous holder died abnormally. On Linux the holder's own release settles against the kernel lock table as §5 describes; the next holder's predecessor rule is unchanged.
1. A holder that will create a process domain while it holds the lock (a job for `run_borrowed` on Windows; the attempt's namespace or job) writes `<lockFile>.predecessor.json` right after acquire and before creating the domain, while it still holds the lock: `{v: 1, domainKind, domainId}`. `domainKind` is `linux-pgroup` (best-effort), `linux-gate` (the gate's process tuple; empty iff `judge(tuple) == dead`), `windows-job` (a named Job Object) or `macos-tree` (a tree root tuple; best-effort). The record is written through a temp file and a rename. A missing record means the holder handed off after proving empty, or created no domain.
2. The next holder, after it holds the kernel lock, reads the record and asks the driver whether the domain is empty. Empty, or unopenable but proven empty: proceed. Not empty: kill the whole domain at once; never wait for it to drain.
3. Then wait at most `killWaitMs` (`lock.predecessorKillWaitMs`, default 2000 ms; measured a few ms) for the killed processes to be signaled. Domain empty: proceed. Deadline passed, or the kill was refused: release the kernel lock and return `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)` naming the domain; doctor shows that domain.
4. When the caller restricts `resource.predecessorKinds` (Node acquire params, Rust `Resource.predecessor_kinds`), acquisition checks that policy **under the kernel lock before ordinary predecessor cleanup**. Execution permits only `linux-gate` and `windows-job` for custody successors; it refuses best-effort or unknown records as `custody-predecessor-unknown` and preserves the worktree. There is no unlocked admission precheck: a busy kernel lock returns `dispatch-in-flight` on every platform before record policy is evaluated.
5. A holder that proceeded and will create a domain itself overwrites the record before creating it. A record with `v != 1`, or an unreadable record, is never deleted or ignored: acquire returns `held (predecessor-domain-not-empty)` with the raw record.

Why kill at once rather than wait for the domain to drain: a drain only helps a holder that was allowed to leave processes running after release, and step 0 forbids that. The second Windows measurement showed every contender waiting the full 2000 ms before terminating; killing at once brings the crash path down to a few milliseconds (p50 5.9 ms, p95 6.9 ms over 50 runs). A holder that violates step 0 on purpose has its leftover killed by the next holder: that is the holder's defect, and `lock-borrow-vectors` catches the known vectors.

`linux-gate` is judged by `judge(gate) == dead` and ended by SIGKILL by identity. On Linux `run_borrowed` declares no predecessor record; it kills the borrowed child's process group, descendants and escaped description holders under §5's refined rule, each signaled by identity. Direct pre-exec children of the holder outside the borrow group are waited and re-checked, never killed. Domain cleanup fails with a named error `borrow-leftover-not-killed` and the pid when one survives the deadline. On macOS the leftovers are the child's process group. `macos-tree` stays contract only until the run supervisor's macOS containment lands. `windows-job` is implemented, as section 8.1 says.

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: ### 8.1 Windows: borrowing in a named job
docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.sectionText:
### 8.1 Windows: borrowing in a named job

Plan and decisions: [plan 4.4b](../../../plans/261017-1256-windows-lockfileex-driver-and-macos-handoff/plan.md). The owner-machine probe that fixed the empty rule: [probe report](../../../plans/reports/probe-261017-0710-windows-predecessor-all-owners-dead-race.md); the review that shaped the views and the Node helper: [red-team](../../../plans/reports/red-team-261017-1330-windows-lockfileex-driver-plan-review.md).

- **Why not a handle.** A child that inherits a `LockFileEx` handle does not hold the lock, and the lock is released when the locking process dies. So `run_borrowed` on Windows never lends the lock: the locking process keeps holding it and runs the child inside a job it creates (`Local\fgos-borrow-<lock>-<pid>-<creation>-<counter>`, `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, no breakaway). The child gets `FGOS_LOCK_JOB=<lock name>:<job name>`. A hook accepts it as the borrower (`--borrowed-check`) only when the env names this lock and a job, the predecessor record names that job and a holder tuple, the hook process is in the job, and the recorded holder is in its ancestor chain with the lock still held.
- **Record shape.** `domainKind: windows-job`, `domainId = {job, sessionId, declaredAt, holder: {host, pid, startTime}, keeper: {host, pid, startTime} | null}`, `v` stays 1. `declaredAt` and `startTime` are decimal FILETIME strings; `keeper` is filled by rewriting the record right after the keeper's ack, before any member exists. A string `domainId` parses to nothing, so it stays fail closed.
- **What the child inherits.** `std::process::Command` always passes `bInheritHandles = TRUE`, so a holder written with it would hand every inheritable handle it owns to git, its hooks and the keeper. Both the borrowed child and the keeper are started by `fgos_process::platform::windows_spawn::spawn` instead: `CreateProcessW` with `STARTUPINFOEXW` and `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST`, so the child inherits the copies made for its three standard streams (a pipe, `NUL`, a file or the caller's own stream) and nothing else; with no stream handle at all, `bInheritHandles` is `FALSE`. A batch file as the borrowed program is refused (`cmd.exe` quoting is not something this driver takes on); no borrowed command is one.
- **Two views of the domain.** The **job view** (release rule and keeper): `ActiveProcesses == 0` and every member named by the job's pid list or by a Toolhelp scan for `IsProcessInJob` is signaled. The **contender view** (`admit`, after the kernel lock is held): a live recorded holder released normally, so the job view decides and only `TerminateJobObject` ever runs; a dead holder gives the union of the job list, the in-job scan and the holder's descendants created at or after `declaredAt` (minus the keeper), re-read on every poll. A pid that is live but cannot be opened keeps the domain not empty. A job that does not open falls back to the tree source with two consecutive quiet snapshots. In that fallback, a process created at or after `declaredAt` whose parent has left the snapshot (or whose pid now belongs to a newer process), and its descendants, are also waited for, for 200 ms after the job was first found gone (a one-shot window; nothing new is named after it closes): a member of a closed job whose parent already exited is no longer reachable from the holder and is still tearing down (measured on Windows CI: a live git pid named by no source, one in about 150 rounds). A holder pid that now belongs to a newer process ends the clause (the holder died a while ago, nothing is tearing down). The 200 ms window is a timing assumption: a member whose teardown outlasts it and that no other source names could still slip, and the owner's 500-repeat gate is the test for it. They are only waited for, never signaled, because an unrelated orphan looks the same. A record of another session is `NotEmpty` with reason `predecessor-other-session`. The contract is [`predecessor.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/predecessor.v1.json) `windowsJobViews`.
- **Keeper.** The locking process spawns `job-keeper` before the job has a member and keeps it outside the job. It exits only when the holder has said `finished` (or its handle is signaled) and the job view is empty, polling every 50 ms with the list and count only. A crash during a borrowed git commit therefore costs about 120-170 ms at the next acquire.
- **`lock-hold` route.** Node cannot call `LockFileEx`, so on Windows it starts one `fgos internal lock-hold` helper per held lock ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/internal-route.lock-hold.v1.json)). Node and the helper talk through files in a private work directory (`ready.json`, `req-<n>.json`, `started-<n>.json`, `result-<n>.json`, output logs), never stdin, because libuv queues pipe writes until the loop turns and `Atomics.wait` blocks the loop. Release is `TerminateProcess` of the helper plus a bounded wait. Parent death during a borrow ends the job at once.
- **Helper roles.** The crate API takes `HelperExe`. Production passes the running executable; tests pass `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_...")`. Roles (`probe-holder`, `job-keeper`) are entered as `fgos internal holder-lock-helper <role>` and as the hidden `fgctl internal holder-lock-helper <role>`, so the `fgctl` gate never runs anything under the candidate release.
- **Windows borrow-vector assertion.** The four vector names and the sibling check are the same. Each background command writes its Windows pid; the vector opens its own `SYNCHRONIZE` handle to it and asserts the handle is signaled when `run_borrowed` returns. The check does not use the driver's own empty rule, and it does not rely on `probe == Free`, which is trivially true on Windows.
- **Doctor.** `lock-holders` judges a `windows-job` record with the read-only `fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state <lockFile>` (one contender-view pass, never kills): `empty` and `absent` are fine, `not-empty` and `unknown` warn with the domain and the reason (for example `predecessor-other-session`). `linux-gate` and `macos-tree` records keep the Node `judge()` path.
- **macOS unchanged.** The `flock` driver and the activation gate are as before; `macos-tree` containment is not part of this work.
- **Fences on Windows.** The quiesce scan stays unsupported there (Toolhelp has no command line), so fences use the attested path of `lock-fences`.
- **CI and gate.** `.github/workflows/holder-lock-cross-platform.yml` runs the Rust and Node tests on `windows-latest` and `macos-latest`. The acceptance gate is the 500-repeat predecessor stress run on the owner's machine (`apps/fgos/tests/windows_predecessor_stress.rs`).

Async fd borrows may overlap, but their successful returns are not independent: a completed borrow waits for protected siblings up to `killWaitMs` and fails closed if any remain. The private owning handle records live sibling borrow roots and passes them both to the existing async drain (`--protected-roots`) and into native loans; Rust drains protect their process groups and descendants from signals. A drain snapshot refuses starting another async/synchronous borrow or minting a native loan with retryable `borrow-drain-in-progress`, before spawn. This bounded refusal is contention, not an authority failure. After the sweep returns, a caller may retry admission. A native Git call overlapping a live async sibling can likewise fail closed at drain without killing that sibling or retrying a Git effect. Escaped descendants of the completed borrow retain the existing cleanup rule.

- **Why not a handle.** A child that inherits a `LockFileEx` handle does not hold the lock, and the lock is released when the locking process dies. So `run_borrowed` on Windows never lends the lock: the locking process keeps holding it and runs the child inside a job it creates (`Local\fgos-borrow-<lock>-<pid>-<creation>-<counter>`, `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, no breakaway). The child gets `FGOS_LOCK_JOB=<lock name>:<job name>`. A hook accepts it as the borrower (`--borrowed-check`) only when the env names this lock and a job, the predecessor record names that job and a holder tuple, the hook process is in the job, and the recorded holder is in its ancestor chain with the lock still held.
- **Record shape.** `domainKind: windows-job`, `domainId = {job, sessionId, declaredAt, holder: {host, pid, startTime}, keeper: {host, pid, startTime} | null}`, `v` stays 1. `declaredAt` and `startTime` are decimal FILETIME strings; `keeper` is filled by rewriting the record right after the keeper's ack, before any member exists. A string `domainId` parses to nothing, so it stays fail closed.
- **What the child inherits.** `std::process::Command` always passes `bInheritHandles = TRUE`, so a holder written with it would hand every inheritable handle it owns to git, its hooks and the keeper. Both the borrowed child and the keeper are started by `fgos_process::platform::windows_spawn::spawn` instead: `CreateProcessW` with `STARTUPINFOEXW` and `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST`, so the child inherits the copies made for its three standard streams (a pipe, `NUL`, a file or the caller's own stream) and nothing else; with no stream handle at all, `bInheritHandles` is `FALSE`. A batch file as the borrowed program is refused (`cmd.exe` quoting is not something this driver takes on); no borrowed command is one.
- **Two views of the domain.** The **job view** (release rule and keeper): `ActiveProcesses == 0` and every member named by the job's pid list or by a Toolhelp scan for `IsProcessInJob` is signaled. The **contender view** (`admit`, after the kernel lock is held): a live recorded holder released normally, so the job view decides and only `TerminateJobObject` ever runs; a dead holder gives the union of the job list, the in-job scan and the holder's descendants created at or after `declaredAt` (minus the keeper), re-read on every poll. A pid that is live but cannot be opened keeps the domain not empty. A job that does not open falls back to the tree source with two consecutive quiet snapshots. In that fallback, a process created at or after `declaredAt` whose parent has left the snapshot (or whose pid now belongs to a newer process), and its descendants, are also waited for, for 200 ms after the job was first found gone (a one-shot window; nothing new is named after it closes): a member of a closed job whose parent already exited is no longer reachable from the holder and is still tearing down (measured on Windows CI: a live git pid named by no source, one in about 150 rounds). A holder pid that now belongs to a newer process ends the clause (the holder died a while ago, nothing is tearing down). The 200 ms window is a timing assumption: a member whose teardown outlasts it and that no other source names could still slip, and the owner's 500-repeat gate is the test for it. They are only waited for, never signaled, because an unrelated orphan looks the same. A record of another session is `NotEmpty` with reason `predecessor-other-session`. The contract is [`predecessor.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/predecessor.v1.json) `windowsJobViews`.
- **Keeper.** The locking process spawns `job-keeper` before the job has a member and keeps it outside the job. It exits only when the holder has said `finished` (or its handle is signaled) and the job view is empty, polling every 50 ms with the list and count only. A crash during a borrowed git commit therefore costs about 120-170 ms at the next acquire.
- **`lock-hold` route.** Node cannot call `LockFileEx`, so on Windows it starts one `fgos internal lock-hold` helper per held lock ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/internal-route.lock-hold.v1.json)). Node and the helper talk through files in a private work directory (`ready.json`, `req-<n>.json`, `started-<n>.json`, `result-<n>.json`, output logs), never stdin, because libuv queues pipe writes until the loop turns and `Atomics.wait` blocks the loop. Release is `TerminateProcess` of the helper plus a bounded wait. Parent death during a borrow ends the job at once.
- **Helper roles.** The crate API takes `HelperExe`. Production passes the running executable; tests pass `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_...")`. Roles (`probe-holder`, `job-keeper`) are entered as `fgos internal holder-lock-helper <role>` and as the hidden `fgctl internal holder-lock-helper <role>`, so the `fgctl` gate never runs anything under the candidate release.
- **Windows borrow-vector assertion.** The four vector names and the sibling check are the same. Each background command writes its Windows pid; the vector opens its own `SYNCHRONIZE` handle to it and asserts the handle is signaled when `run_borrowed` returns. The check does not use the driver's own empty rule, and it does not rely on `probe == Free`, which is trivially true on Windows.
- **Doctor.** `lock-holders` judges a `windows-job` record with the read-only `fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state <lockFile>` (one contender-view pass, never kills): `empty` and `absent` are fine, `not-empty` and `unknown` warn with the domain and the reason (for example `predecessor-other-session`). `linux-gate` and `macos-tree` records keep the Node `judge()` path.
- **macOS unchanged.** The `flock` driver and the activation gate are as before; `macos-tree` containment is not part of this work.
- **Fences on Windows.** The quiesce scan stays unsupported there (Toolhelp has no command line), so fences use the attested path of `lock-fences`.
- **CI and gate.** `.github/workflows/holder-lock-cross-platform.yml` runs the Rust and Node tests on `windows-latest` and `macos-latest`. The acceptance gate is the 500-repeat predecessor stress run on the owner's machine (`apps/fgos/tests/windows_predecessor_stress.rs`).

docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md.text: Async fd borrows may overlap, but their successful returns are not independent: a completed borrow waits for protected siblings up to `killWaitMs` and fails closed if any remain. The private owning handle records live sibling borrow roots and passes them both to the existing async drain (`--protected-roots`) and into native loans; Rust drains protect their process groups and descendants from signals. A drain snapshot refuses starting another async/synchronous borrow or minting a native loan with retryable `borrow-drain-in-progress`, before spawn. This bounded refusal is contention, not an authority failure. After the sweep returns, a caller may retry admission. A native Git call overlapping a live async sibling can likewise fail closed at drain without killing that sibling or retrying a Git effect. Escaped descendants of the completed borrow retain the existing cleanup rule.
